expected_symptom: -MD/-MF (or -M) silences error output during a normal compile, forcing the reporter to compile twice.
reviewed_by: gpt-5.3-codex (independent batch-019 step-10 review; applied selectively at collation)
summary: Reproduces, and the mechanism is worse than reported: dxc doesn't just fail to print diagnostics under -M/-MD/-MF, it reports a successful compile (exit 0) for source that would otherwise be rejected. All three flags set the single opts.DumpDependencies bit (lib/DxcSupport/HLSLOptions.cpp), which routes DxcContext::Compile through clang::PreprocessOnlyAction (tools/clang/tools/dxcompiler/dxcompilerobj.cpp, DumpDependencies branch) instead of the normal compile action -- no Parser or Sema ever runs, so no parse/semantic diagnostic can be produced, and the unified hasErrorOccurred() check finds nothing. Preprocessor-level errors (missing #include) still surface, since the preprocessor is what actually runs; only parser/Sema diagnostics (undeclared identifiers, missing semicolons) are lost. Confirmed with three controls: same source without -MD/-MF is correctly rejected; a bad #include still fails under -MD/-MF; a pure syntax error (missing semicolon) also silently 'succeeds' under -MD/-MF. Always-repro's from v1.7.2207 through v1.9.2607 (the full probeable range); earlier releases correctly rejected -MD as an invalid-probe (option did not exist, introduced by #4017, merged 2021-12-21). CE corroborates: https://godbolt.org/z/s4Mcsxj66 shows the same source erroring on one pane and reporting <No output file> at exit 0 on the other.
title: Dumping header dependencies to file prevents error output
